Messages.Author: dude_PL
Messages.Body:
I voted taste of vitae, although disarm would be my next choice. Not because of them being "broken" (I simply don't like them, I never have, but that's another story), but because of lack of consistency. Suddenly they have no vitae (although theft of vitae works just fine) or no hands to rip off. This is just plainly stupid.

On the side note, ally decks are a pain for combat decks purely because of taste of vitae not working. I've played around with orgy of blood, but it's very situational and - more often than not - a dead card slot.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
I would say "all of thoses cited".

Notice that all choice except one are combat card. Notice that combat already have polyvalency problesm. Notice that allies are also "immune" to aggravated damage. Notice that the two combat style that work well are near unaffected by the difference between allies and vampires.

Messages.Author: Dorrinal
Messages.Body: Gaining a blood advantage is necessary in a lot of combat decks - it can fuel bloat via masters and sometimes keep a vampire out of torpor for one more turn. Many decks use taste of vitae to get that advantage. But it adds complexity and uncertainty to those decks that need it, partly because it typically takes up a lot more deck space than the other options. The one card that would benefit other decks the most in terms of blood and card flow is Taste of Vitae, and that is my choice.

Messages.Author: mongrel222
Messages.Body:
For me, it's a three way tie between Haven Uncovered, Fame and Taste of Vitae. Those are stock cards in many combat decks across many disciplines, so it's more ruinous to the game to have those cards busted rather than particular discipline cards.

If really forced to choose from those 3, I think I'd choose Fame (obviously fixed so that "incapacitated" replaces "torpor" when played on Imbued). Give the combat deck _some_ form of ousting strategy rather than just bleed for 1.

Messages.Author: TryDeflectingThisGrapple
Messages.Body:
Clearly Taste of Vitae. Theft works, even on non-mortal allies. There's no thematic or mechanical reason why Taste shouldn't too.

Since Taste is the gas on which most combat engines run, allowing it to work on allies removes one of the many roadblocks combat decks face.

Runner up votes for Disarm & Decap - surely allies have arms and heads to be ripped off.

Messages.Author: jhattara
Messages.Body:
Thematically there is a good reason why Taste of Vitae doesn't work on allies: vampire vitae is more potent than mortal blood. In the RPG 13th generation vampire holds 10 pints of vitae that are 10 blood points (roughly same concentration as human blood), while a 7th generation vampire holds 10 pints of vitae that are 20 blood points (roughly twice as concentrated). Also some elder vampires can not be nourished by mere blood, but need vitae to sustain themselves.

As for Obediece, Decapitate and Disarm... Thematically there is no reason why these shouldn't work for imbued (as well as other allies) equally as well as with vampires. I voted for Disarm, because that would be probably the most beneficial.

I vote "Taste of Vitae" for the reasons stated by Dorrinal.

Decapitate should be a candidate. Why shouldn't you be able to burn the imbued before the ambulance hauls them off to the hospital?

Disarm should not be applicable to Imbued. You remove a vampire's arm, and they can heal the wound. Remove a mortal's arm and they die a horrible death. Even if they were to survive a Disarm, a mortal cannot regrow their arms, and would be permanently "incapacitated."

Messages.Author: ReverendRevolver
Messages.Body:
i voted disarm. taste of vitae is your vamp tasting the opponents vitae (vamp blood, supernatural "juice" that fuels their power) so imbued, while supernatural, are about as high in vitae content as a turnip is.

imbued have arms and heads that should be able to get ripped off. i voted disarm because i think its better than decapitate (i at least pay it and see it played more, i just wish it gave you a melee weapon for later use (you know, so you could rip someones arm off and beat people with it...)

anyway, jake washington is an imbued in a wheel chair, and i'm told that fluff wise he eventually recovers and is a-ok.
so, an imbued should be able to get their arm ripped off and live, but since they have life not blood, they shouldn't be able to regrow the arm. i mean, they aren't lizards regrowing tails afterall, they aren't as regeneratively awesome as vamps or werwolves.
but there is not a drop of canon or design related evidence that imbued shouldn't be able to get decapitated or disarmed.
taste is out, for fluff reasons. obedience should effect them, but lets assume that the hunter net protects them from such a lazy use of dominate. other things could be arguably vamp oriented, but the only reason disarm and decapitate can't hit imbued is they were printed before imbued existed.

and i agree that allies or a ghoul, mortal, werewolf, mage, zombie, mummy, and even animal persuasion should be able to do things as dawn ops, so if a vamp wants to block, they can deal with sunlight.

Messages.Author: AaronC
Messages.Body:
I voted for Obedience. All the Dominate cards that don't affect allies should affect them: Seduction, Redirection, Mind Rape, and others (?).

Of course, I think that Dominate cards (including Deflection) should never be usable on older vampires, that's how crazy, messed-up addicted I am to the source material (and it would incidentally be a nice way to nerf Dominate a bit).

I don't understand why Graverobbing is on the poll, however. Allies don't go to torpor. Does the poll imply that Graverobbing would affect allies in the ash heap?

BTW, Jake Washington's legs were healed by another Imbued using the level 4 Vision power "Restore". Self-healing is not a power inherent to all Imbued.

I'd say : none of them.
But before answering, I'd like to know if the vampires themselves are aware of imbued existence ? Until now I guesses that most of them don't see anything surnatural when a human comes and intercept/defies them. They just see a foolish human and if something a bit surnatural happens, they simply think some other forces are at work, or maybe the human was just lucky... They dont' think about powers or virtues, because it's a bit out of their reach. Mehuselahs (players) do, but not their minions...

After a combat I'd understand a vampire who takes time to decapitate another vampire to make sure he never stands in his way again, but after dispatching a puny human who seems dead cold, why the need to stop and tear him apart ? After all, there's nothing to fear from an unlucky mortal bystander.
So Disarm and decapitate should not work on them simply because a vampire would not bother : what is dead is dead.
